profile.headline: Computer Science Student | C++ | C# | Python | Agile | Active TS/SCI | Army Veteran | Linux
profile.summary:
Cleared Army intelligence professional transitioning into software engineering. Former Geospatial Intelligence Analyst with experience in real time intelligence collection operations.

Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science and GIS at the University of North Texas. I have hands-on experience building projects in C++ (preferred), C, C#, Python, and JavaScript, with additional experience in HTML/CSS and Agile development practices.

With a background in intelligence operations and an active clearance, I’m interested in software engineering roles supporting defense systems and mission critical software platforms.

Clearance: Active TS/SCI
Languages & Tools: C++, C, C#, JavaScript, Python, HTML/CSS, Git, Qt creator, ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online
Academic Achievements: 4x President’s List | Strong in Data Structures, and OOP
Interests: Software Development | Embedded Systems | Data Visualization

projects.title: Saferide - Ridesharing Application
projects.description:
Designed and developed the backend for a ridesharing application using C# and .NET, focusing on system architecture and scalability.

Architected the overall system and created a class diagram to model riders, drivers, and ride lifecycle workflows using object-oriented design principles.

Implemented a dynamic driver-rider matchmaking system using the Google Maps Route Matrix API to assign the closest available driver based on real-time travel duration (ETA).

Developed RESTful API controllers to support user authentication (registration, login, logout) and ride request workflows.

Integrated Google Maps Routes API to compute trip distance, estimated time of arrival, and routing data, including encoded polylines for frontend map visualization.

Utilized asynchronous programming (async/await) to efficiently handle external API calls.

Designed a modular backend architecture with clear separation of concerns (controllers, services, models) to support maintainability and future scalability.

Collaborated in an Agile team environment using Git for version control, feature branching, and merge conflict resolution.
